stem.en: A block moves along a smooth horizontal floor from $x = 0$ to $x = 4\ \mathrm{m}$ while a single horizontal force acts on it. The force is not steady. It rises linearly from 0 N at $x = 0$ to 50 N at $x = 1\ \mathrm{m}$, holds at 50 N until $x = 3\ \mathrm{m}$, then falls linearly back to 0 N at $x = 4\ \mathrm{m}$. Find the work done by this force over the whole 4 m, in joules.

graph.a11yCaption: Force against displacement: the force rises from 0 N to 50 N over the first metre, stays at 50 N until 3 m, then falls back to 0 N at 4 m. The region under the line is shaded.

explanation.en: Read the work off the force-displacement graph as the area under the curve: a triangle from 0 to 1 m, a rectangle from 1 m to 3 m, and a triangle from 3 m to 4 m. That is 1/2 x 1 x 50 = 25 J, plus 2 x 50 = 100 J, plus 1/2 x 1 x 50 = 25 J, giving 150 J.

hints.en: Split the shaded region into pieces whose areas you already know: two triangles and one rectangle.
Each triangle has area one half of base times height: 1/2 x 1 m x 50 N. The flat middle part is a rectangle 2 m wide and 50 N tall.
